mainTopic: Whether a thought during שחיטה about a later עבודה counts (רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, רב נחמן and רבה), and רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם שלא לשמו is invalid.
overview: This amud opens with a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about someone who slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה. רבי יוחנן forbids the animal: a thought during one עבודה can affect another, and we learn חוץ from פנים. ריש לקיש permits it on both counts. The גמרא explains why we need their argument both here and in the earlier קרבן case of שלא לשמה. רב ירמיה supports רבי יוחנן with a קל וחומר, which is broken twice and finally rebuilt by רב אשי using a thought לשם פלוני. רבי אילא supports ריש לקיש from the extra verse about זריקה, and that proof goes through a back-and-forth of challenges and answers. רבה then retracts and agrees with רב נחמן that a חטאת slaughtered with a plan to do the זריקה שלא לשמה is invalid, because of רב אשי's קל וחומר. Finally, the גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם brought שלא לשמו is also invalid. רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר trade comparisons to חטאת and פסח, and רבי יהושע's next reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughtering with intent for idol worship: רבי יוחנן forbids
steps.stepSummary: The case is someone who slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה. רבי יוחנן rules the animal is forbidden, because intent can carry from one עבודה to another, and we learn 'outside' from 'inside'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters an animal planning to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for idol worship, רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden. Intent during one service can affect a different service, and we learn laws for outside the מקדש from laws inside the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new case about slaughtering for עבודה זרה and gives רבי יוחנן's ruling that the animal is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter itself was not for the idol. Only the later acts (sprinkling, burning) were planned for it. רבי יוחנן still forbids it for two reasons: intent during the שחיטה about a later עבודה counts, and we may learn this idol-worship law (which applies anywhere, 'outside') from the rules of intent for קרבנות 'inside' the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Forbidden (here: forbidden to benefit from the animal)
Intent during one service can apply to a different service
We learn (derive)
Laws that apply outside the מקדש learned from laws that apply inside it

steps.confusionAlert: The person did not slaughter for the idol. He slaughtered normally but planned to do the later steps for the idol. That is exactly why there is a question.

phrases.english: One who slaughters the animal

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: in order to sprinkle its blood for idol worship,
or to burn its fat for idol worship –
Rabbi Yochanan says: it is forbidden;
we can have intent from one service to another service,
and we derive outside from inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה עַל מְנָת לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel dispute to the earlier one about intent שלא לשמה, now in the area of עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, an animal slaughtered with intent to sprinkle its blood or burn its fat for עבודה זרה is forbidden. Intent carries from one עבודה to another, and חוץ is learned from פנים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש permits the animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees and says the animal is permitted. Intent does not carry from one עבודה to another, and we do not learn 'outside' from 'inside'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says it is permitted. Intent during one service does not affect another service, and we do not learn laws for outside from laws for inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's opposing ruling: the animal is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש rejects both of רבי יוחנן's reasons. He holds that a plan about a later act does not affect the שחיטה. Even if it did inside the מקדש, he holds that idol-worship law cannot be learned from the rules of קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
We do not count intent (from one service to another)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: it is permitted;
we cannot have intent from one service to another service,
and we do not derive outside from inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רבי יוחנן in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, the animal is permitted. There is no מחשבה from one עבודה to another, and חוץ is not learned from פנים.

steps.title: Why the idol-worship dispute alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why both disputes are needed. If we only had the עבודה זרה dispute, we might think ריש לקיש permits only there, because he won't learn חוץ from פנים. Inside the מקדש, learning פנים from פנים, he might agree with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had taught us only this case (idol worship), we would say ריש לקיש says his view only here. But in a case of inside learned from inside, we might say he agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why record the same dispute twice? It starts with the first half of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the idol-worship case, ריש לקיש has an extra reason to permit: you can't learn חוץ from פנים. That extra reason is missing in the earlier קרבן case of intent שלא לשמה, where everything is 'inside'. So from the idol case alone, we could not know he also permits in the קרבן case.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it had taught us
Inside from inside: learning one מקדש law from another
He agrees with him
I might say

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only in this case –
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the idol-worship case we just learned.

phrases.english: in this case Reish Lakish says his view,
but in a case of inside from inside
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier case on the דף: slaughtering a קרבן with intent to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה.

phrases.english: I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the dispute in steps 1-2 does not make the earlier קרבן dispute unnecessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the קרבן dispute, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן inside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קרבן dispute is needed to show that ריש לקיש disagrees even פנים מפנים.

steps.title: Why the Temple dispute alone would not be enough, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the earlier קרבן dispute, we might think רבי יוחנן forbids only inside the מקדש. In the idol case, he might agree with ריש לקיש that חוץ is not learned from פנים. So both disputes are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had taught us only that case (the קרבן), we would say רבי יוחנן says his view only there. But in the other case (idol worship), I might say he agrees with ריש לקיש. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of its answer and concludes that both disputes are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קרבן case, רבי יוחנן only needs one idea: intent carries from one עבודה to another. In the idol case, he also needs to learn חוץ מפנים, which is a bigger step. So only the idol-worship dispute shows he goes that far, and each dispute teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: In that other case
They are both necessary

steps.whatToRemember: The same dispute appears twice because each case teaches something new. The קרבן case shows that ריש לקיש rejects intent from one עבודה to another even inside the מקדש. The idol case shows that רבי יוחנן learns חוץ מפנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two אמוראים disagree on two separate ideas: מחשבה from one עבודה to another, and learning חוץ from פנים. Each case is needed to show their full positions.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this case –
phrases.notes: Now 'this case' means the earlier קרבן case of intent שלא לשמה.

phrases.english: in this case Rabbi Yochanan says his view,
but in that other case
I might say he agrees with Reish Lakish;
they are both necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 3 by giving the reverse side and concluding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both disputes are necessary. Each one shows a part of one אמורא's view that we could not learn from the other case.

steps.title: רב דימי reports support for each side
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says that רב ירמיה brought support for רבי יוחנן and רבי אילא brought support for ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רב ירמיה brought an argument to support רבי יוחנן, and רבי אילא brought one to support ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next part. It tells us two אמוראים will each try to back up one side of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only had two opinions and why both disputes are needed. Now the גמרא looks for actual proofs. One proof is announced for each side, and the details come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings)
To support him

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Rav Yirmeya raises an argument
to support Rabbi Yochanan,
and Rabbi Ila to support Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: מֵתִיב רַב יִרְמְיָה לְסַיּוֹעֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that both disputes are needed, the גמרא now looks for proofs for each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two proofs exist: רב ירמיה for רבי יוחנן, רבי אילא for ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רב ירמיה's קל וחומר for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: From חוץ לזמנו, where a thought about the later זריקה ruins the קרבן, רב ירמיה argues that the same must be true for שלא לשמו, which is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at חוץ לזמנו. If he says 'I am slaughtering beyond its time,' the animal is still כשר. Yet if he slaughters planning to sprinkle the blood beyond its time, it is פסול. Now look at שלא לשמו, where even saying 'I am slaughtering not for its sake' makes it פסול. Surely if he slaughters planning to sprinkle the blood שלא לשמו, it should be פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה builds a קל וחומר to show that a thought during שחיטה about the זריקה counts for שלא לשמו. That is what רבי יוחנן holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חוץ לזמנו, a wrong thought about the שחיטה itself does nothing, yet a thought about the later זריקה does ruin the קרבן. With שלא לשמו, even a wrong thought about the שחיטה itself ruins it, so it looks stricter. So a thought about the זריקה should surely ruin it too, which means the thought carries from one עבודה to another.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... is it not logical? (the wording of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר)
Beyond its set time (the thought that makes a קרבן פִּגּוּל)
Not for its own sake, meaning as a different kind of קרבן
Fit / unfit

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya, to support Rabbi Yochanan:
Just as in a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering beyond its time," it is fit,
yet if he slaughtered it in order to sprinkle its blood
beyond its time, it is unfit;
then a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering not for its sake," it is unfit,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחָטוֹ עַל מְנָת לִזְרוֹק דָּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
phrases.english: if he slaughtered it in order to sprinkle its blood not for its sake,
is it not logical that it should be unfit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִרְמְיָה לְסַיּוֹעֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאִם אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the support for רבי יוחנן that was announced in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a thought of שלא לשמו during שחיטה about the זריקה makes the קרבן פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from חוץ לזמנו, where a thought about the זריקה ruins the קרבן even though a thought about the שחיטה itself does not.

steps.title: רבא בר אהילאי: חוץ לזמנו is stricter because of כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי breaks the קל וחומר. חוץ לזמנו has its own strictness, כרת, so you cannot learn שלא לשמו from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אהילאי objected: What about חוץ לזמנו? It is special, because it carries כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי attacks רב ירמיה's proof. The case it was built on has a strictness that שלא לשמו does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the starting case is clearly the lighter one. Eating a קרבן made פיגול by a חוץ לזמנו thought carries כרת, but שלא לשמו does not. So חוץ לזמנו may be stricter in its own way, and maybe that is the only reason a thought about the זריקה counts there.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, attacks the argument
What about X? It is special because... (a פִּירְכָא, breaking a קל וחומר)
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פִּגּוּל

phrases.english: Rava bar Ahilai objects to it:
What about "beyond its time"?
It is special, since it carries כרת!
phrases.notes: Eating meat made פיגול by this thought carries כרת. A קרבן made פסול by שלא לשמו does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר אֲהִילַאי: מָה לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, שֶׁכֵּן כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the starting case of רב ירמיה's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ירמיה's קל וחומר from חוץ לזמנו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חוץ לזמנו carries כרת, so it is not clearly lighter than שלא לשמו, and the קל וחומר fails.

steps.title: רבא בר אהילאי rebuilds the proof using חוץ למקומו
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי says רב ירמיה really meant חוץ למקומו, which has no כרת. The same קל וחומר works from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא בר אהילאי said, this is what he meant: Look at חוץ למקומו. If he says 'I am slaughtering outside its place,' it is כשר. Yet if he slaughters planning to sprinkle the blood outside its place, it is פסול. Now in שלא לשמו, even saying 'I am slaughtering not for its sake' makes it פסול. Surely if he slaughters planning to sprinkle the blood שלא לשמו, it should be פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי fixes the proof he just broke. He swaps חוץ לזמנו for חוץ למקומו so the כרת objection no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a קרבן made פסול by a חוץ למקומו thought has no כרת, so it has no special strictness over שלא לשמו. A thought about the זריקה ruins it, while a thought about the שחיטה itself does not. So for the stricter שלא לשמו, a thought about the זריקה should surely count, which supports רבי יוחנן again.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the first version for a better one)
This is what he meant
Outside its proper place; makes the קרבן פסול, but with no כרת

steps.whatToRemember: רב ירמיה's support for רבי יוחנן is a קל וחומר: if a thought about the זריקה counts for חוץ למקומו, it surely counts for the stricter שלא לשמו. The version with חוץ לזמנו fails because of כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about the place or time itself. It uses those cases only to show that a thought during שחיטה about the later זריקה can count.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava bar Ahilai said,
this is what he is saying:
Just as in a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering outside its place," it is fit,
yet if he slaughtered it in order to sprinkle its blood
outside its place, it is unfit;
then a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering not for its sake," it is unfit,

phrases.aramaic: [שְׁחָטוֹ עַל מְנָת] לִזְרוֹק דָּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ –
phrases.english: if he slaughtered it in order to sprinkle its blood not for its sake,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, so it matches the earlier version of the proof.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should be unfit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר אֲהִילַאי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כרת objection by restating רב ירמיה's proof with חוץ למקומו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the proof: replacing the starting case with one that has no כרת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ירמיה's קל וחומר was built from חוץ לזמנו, which could be broken because of כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is built from חוץ למקומו, which has no כרת, so the כרת objection no longer applies. רב אשי challenges this version in the next step.

steps.title: רב אשי Challenges the Comparison to חוץ למקומו
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that you cannot learn שלא לשמו from חוץ למקומו, because חוץ למקומו applies to every קרבן, while שלא לשמו ruins only a פסח and a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: חוץ למקומו is special, because it applies to all offerings. Can you say the same about שלא לשמו, which ruins only a פסח and a חטאת?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the fixed-up קל וחומר from Step 8. He shows that חוץ למקומו is stronger than שלא לשמו in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is weaker in every way. חוץ למקומו covers every kind of קרבן, while שלא לשמו actually ruins only a פסח and a חטאת. So חוץ למקומו has its own strength, and the קל וחומר breaks again.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it (attacks the argument)
Applies, is in effect
Slaughtered offerings (all kinds of קרבנות)
The קרבן פסח and the sin offering, the two offerings that שלא לשמו actually ruins

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: other קרבנות brought שלא לשמו are still valid. They just don't count for the owner's obligation. Only a פסח and a חטאת become fully פסול.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to it:
What about a thought of outside its place?
It is special, because it applies to all offerings.
Will you say the same about "not for its sake"
which applies only to a פסח and a חטאת?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corrected קל וחומר from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from חוץ למקומו to שלא לשמו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case (חוץ למקומו) has its own strength, because it applies to all זבחים, so it cannot serve as the weaker side of a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רב אשי Rebuilds the Proof from a Thought for Another Person
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רב ירמיה really compared to a thought "for the sake of so-and-so." That thought during שחיטה is harmless, yet it ruins the קרבן when it is about the זריקה. So שלא לשמו, which ruins even during שחיטה, should surely ruin when it is about the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said this is what רב ירמיה meant. Saying "I am slaughtering for so-and-so" during שחיטה leaves the קרבן valid. Still, slaughtering in order to sprinkle the blood for so-and-so makes it פסול. Saying "I am slaughtering not for its sake" already makes it פסול. Then slaughtering in order to sprinkle not for its sake should surely make it פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new reading of רב ירמיה's proof for רבי יוחנן. This time it uses a source case that cannot be knocked down so easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new weaker case is a thought for another person (לשם פלוני). That thought does nothing during שחיטה itself, yet it ruins the קרבן when it is aimed at the later זריקה. שלא לשמו is stronger, because it ruins even during שחיטה. So a שלא לשמו thought aimed at the זריקה should surely ruin it too, just as רבי יוחנן holds.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
"I am hereby slaughtering"
For the sake of so-and-so (another person)
Isn't it logical? (the closing line of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: After two failed versions, רב אשי's version of רב ירמיה's קל וחומר stands: if a thought for another person about the זריקה ruins the קרבן, then a שלא לשמו thought about the זריקה surely does. This supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
This is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב ירמיה. רב אשי is explaining what his proof really was.

phrases.english: Just as in a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering for the sake of so-and-so," it is valid,

phrases.aramaic: לִזְרוֹק דָּמוֹ (שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ) לְשֵׁם פְּלוֹנִי – פָּסוּל;
phrases.english: yet if he slaughtered in order to sprinkle its blood for the sake of so-and-so, it is invalid;
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, so read it simply as "to sprinkle its blood for so-and-so."

phrases.english: then in a case where, if he said
"I am hereby slaughtering not for their sake," it is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: [שְׁחָטוֹ עַל מְנָת] לִזְרוֹק דָּמָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן –
phrases.english: if he slaughtered it in order to sprinkle their blood not for their sake,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. They make clear the thought happens during the שחיטה.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that it should be invalid?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's own challenge by changing the source case of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the proof's source case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ירמיה's קל וחומר was learned from חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו
steps.terutzMaskana: It was learned from a thought for another person (לשם פלוני), which is weaker than שלא לשמו, so the קל וחומר holds

steps.title: רבי אילא Brings Support for ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא argues that the Torah did not need to write the rule of לשמה about זריקה. It could have been learned from שחיטה and קבלה. So the extra wording must teach that a thought from one עבודה does not carry over to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא, supporting ריש לקיש: The Torah should not have needed to say it about זריקה. We could learn it by a קל וחומר from what שחיטה and קבלה have in common! So for what law did the Torah write it? To teach that a thought during one עבודה does not affect another עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side promised in Step 5. רבי אילא brings his support for ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שחיטה and קבלה are ruined by שלא לשמו, so זריקה could have been learned from them. The Torah wrote it anyway, so the extra wording must teach something new. רבי אילא says it teaches that a thought is only judged within its own עבודה. That means a thought at שחיטה about the זריקה does nothing, just as ריש לקיש says.

keyTerms.meaning: To support him
From what the two cases share
Receiving the blood in a vessel
The Merciful One (the Torah)
Having a thought during one service about another service

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila, to support Reish Lakish:
The Torah should not have said it about sprinkling,
and let it be learned by a קל וחומר
from what slaughter and receiving have in common!
For what law did the Merciful One write it?
To say that one does not have a thought from one service to another service.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִילָא לְסַיּוֹעֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב ירמיה's support for רבי יוחנן to רבי אילא's support for ריש לקיש, as announced in Step 5
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's position that a thought during one עבודה about another עבודה does not ruin the קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah wrote the rule about זריקה even though it could have been learned by a קל וחומר from שחיטה and קבלה

steps.title: רב פפא: The Extra Wording May Teach the Opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes back on רבי אילא. The extra wording about זריקה might teach that a thought from one עבודה does carry over to another, which is רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: But maybe it teaches that a thought does carry over from one service to another!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down רבי אילא's proof. He shows that the extra wording could just as easily mean the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא agrees that the Torah's extra wording teaches something. But nothing forces it to teach a leniency. It could be adding a new way to ruin the קרבן: a thought during one עבודה about another. So the proof for ריש לקיש is not conclusive.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
That one does have such a thought (it does take effect)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא challenges רבי אילא: the extra wording about זריקה could teach the opposite. The next step answers this and restores רבי אילא's proof.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
But perhaps it teaches that one does have a thought from one service to another service!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אילא's reading of the extra wording
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אילא's proof for ריש לקיש from the extra wording about זריקה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra wording does not have to teach a leniency. It could just as well teach that a thought about another עבודה does ruin the קרבן.

steps.title: The verse is not needed to teach carry-over, so it must teach the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי אילא against רב פפא. If carry-over were true, we would already know it from רב אשי's קל וחומר, so the Torah would not need to write it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse could have stayed silent about it, and we would learn it from the קל וחומר of רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's pushback and defends רבי אילא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא suggested that the extra wording about זריקה teaches that a thought carries over from one עבודה to another. But רב אשי's קל וחומר (Step 10) already proves that a שלא לשמה thought about the זריקה ruins the קרבן. A verse would not be written just to teach something a קל וחומר already gives us, so the verse must be teaching the opposite: thoughts do not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a response that tests the other side's claim
Let the verse be silent about it; the Torah would not need to write it
Let it come; we could learn it from another source
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

phrases.english: If so, let the verse be silent about it,
and it would come from the קל וחומר of רב אשי.
phrases.notes: This is the קל וחומר from Step 10, about a thought for the sake of so-and-so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִשְׁתּוֹק קְרָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's pushback (Step 12) and restores רבי אילא's proof (Step 11).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redundancy argument: a verse is not needed for what a קל וחומר already teaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra זריקה wording might teach that a thought carries over from one עבודה to another.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is already known from רב אשי's קל וחומר, so the verse must teach that a thought does not carry over.

steps.title: זריקה cannot be learned from שחיטה and קבלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן refutes רבי אילא's starting point. The verse about זריקה is not extra, because שחיטה and קבלה have stricter features that זריקה does not share.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one refutes it like this: what about those two? They are special, because they must be done in the north, and they are part of the inner חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן would attack רבי אילא's claim that the verse about זריקה is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילא assumed the rule of לשמה for זריקה could have been learned from שחיטה and קבלה. רבי יוחנן says no: in קדשי קדשים, שחיטה and קבלה must be done in the north of the courtyard, and they also happen in the inner חטאות. The זריקה of those inner חטאות is not done on the outer מזבח, so זריקה does not share these features. Since זריקה cannot be learned from them, the Torah needed to write it, and there is no extra wording to learn from.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one; here רבי יוחנן, who disagrees with רבי אילא's approach
Refutes; breaks a comparison by showing a difference
What about these? A standard way to point out what makes the source cases special
Must be done in the north of the Temple courtyard
Inner sin offerings, whose blood is brought inside the Sanctuary

phrases.english: And the other one refutes like this:
phrases.notes: "The other one" is רבי יוחנן, who holds that a thought does carry over.

phrases.english: What about these? They are special, for they require the north,
and they are found in the inner sin offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ פָּרֵיךְ הָכִי: מָה לְהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 restored רבי אילא's proof, this step attacks the proof's starting assumption that the זריקה verse is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילא's claim that לשמה for זריקה could be learned from שחיטה and קבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה and קבלה have stricter features (north, inner חטאות) that זריקה lacks, so the learning fails and the זריקה verse is needed for the basic rule.

steps.title: We are dealing with שלמים, so the stricter features do not matter
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the verses about לשמה are about שלמים. שלמים need no north and are not inner חטאות, so the differences fall away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one would say: right now, at any rate, we are dealing with שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's answer to רבי יוחנן's refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of לשמה is learned from the verses about שלמים. שלמים can be slaughtered anywhere in the courtyard, and they are not inner חטאות. So for שלמים, שחיטה and קבלה have no stricter features, and זריקה could be learned from them. That makes the זריקה wording extra again, and רבי אילא's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at any rate; in the case we are actually discussing
Peace offerings, a lighter קרבן with no north requirement
We are standing; we are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two "ואידך" lines. The first (Step 14) is רבי יוחנן attacking the proof. The second (Step 15) is ריש לקיש defending it.

phrases.english: And the other one would say: now, at any rate,
phrases.notes: This "other one" is ריש לקיש, whose view רבי אילא was supporting.

phrases.english: we are dealing with peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא בִּשְׁלָמִים קַיָּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's refutation in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the context: the verses are about שלמים, where the stricter features do not exist.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זריקה cannot be learned from שחיטה and קבלה because those need the north and appear in inner חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שלמים these features do not apply, so זריקה could be learned and the verse is extra, as רבי אילא said.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: a thought does not carry over from one עבודה to another, because the extra זריקה verse teaches this. רבי יוחנן: the verse is not extra, since זריקה cannot be learned from שחיטה and קבלה.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רבה argue about slaughtering with a שלא לשמה thought about the זריקה
steps.stepSummary: A parallel dispute: someone slaughtered a חטאת for its sake, but planned to do the זריקה not for its sake. רב נחמן says it is invalid. רבה says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if one slaughtered it for its sake, intending to sprinkle its blood not for its sake, רב נחמן said it is invalid, and רבה said it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of a similar dispute between two other אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute: does a thought during שחיטה about the זריקה count? רב נחמן says it does, so the קרבן is ruined. רבה at first says it does not, so the קרבן stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered it for its own sake
Invalid
Valid

phrases.english: It was stated: if one slaughtered it for its sake,
phrases.notes: "It" is a חטאת, which is ruined when done not for its sake.

phrases.english: intending to sprinkle its blood not for its sake,
רב נחמן said: it is invalid,
רבה said: it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שְׁחָטָהּ לִשְׁמָהּ, לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel dispute on the same question discussed by רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: a שלא לשמה thought about the זריקה during שחיטה ruins the חטאת. רבה: it stays valid.

steps.title: רבה changes his mind because of רב אשי's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה takes back his view and agrees with רב נחמן that the קרבן is invalid, because of רב אשי's קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה retracted and agreed with רב נחמן, because of the קל וחומר of רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the dispute ends: רבה accepts רב נחמן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's קל וחומר (Step 10) says this: a thought for the sake of so-and-so does nothing during שחיטה, yet it ruins the קרבן when it is about the זריקה. So a שלא לשמה thought, which ruins even during שחיטה, should surely ruin when it is about the זריקה. This argument convinced רבה, so both now agree the קרבן is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; he took back his opinion
Toward; he came over to the other's view

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבה and רב נחמן agree: slaughtering a חטאת with a plan to do the זריקה שלא לשמה makes it invalid, because of רב אשי's קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב אשי's קל וחומר is strong enough to change an אמורא's ruling, and it settles the dispute in favor of invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבָּה לְגַבֵּי רַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: And רבה retracted and came over to רב נחמן,
because of the קל וחומר of רב אשי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבָּה לְגַבֵּי רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute of Step 16 using the קל וחומר from Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חטאת is invalid; רבה agrees with רב נחמן because of רב אשי's קל וחומר.

steps.title: New topic: רבי אליעזר includes the אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רבי אליעזר says the אשם is also invalid when offered שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the אשם too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting רבי אליעזר's line from the משנה. It is setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only פסח and חטאת become invalid when brought שלא לשמן. רבי אליעזר adds the אשם to that list. Next the גמרא will show where his view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Also, too
Not for its own sake, offered with the wrong intent

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The guilt offering, too.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, he means the אשם is also invalid when brought שלא לשמו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף (אֶת) הָאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב נחמן and רבה discussion and quotes a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, an אשם offered שלא לשמו is invalid.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר compares אשם to חטאת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי אליעזר's reason. Both חטאת and אשם come because of a sin, so the אשם should share the חטאת's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר said, a חטאת comes for a sin and an אשם comes for a sin. Just as a חטאת offered שלא לשמה is invalid, so too an אשם offered שלא לשמו is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the source of רבי אליעזר's view. He compares the אשם to the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument rests on one shared feature: both offerings come to atone for a sin. Since the חטאת is invalid שלא לשמה, he says the אשם must be the same. The next steps test whether this comparison really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Comes because of a sin
Just as... so too... (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer said:
A sin offering comes for a transgression,
and a guilt offering comes for a transgression;
just as a sin offering not for its sake is invalid,
so too a guilt offering not for its sake is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: חַטָּאת בָּאָה עַל חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the משנה's line quoted in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that an אשם שלא לשמו is invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to חטאת, based on the shared feature that both come for a sin.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: חטאת is stricter because its blood goes above
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the comparison. A חטאת has a stricter feature, since its blood is put on the upper part of the מזבח, and the אשם lacks it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No. You can say this about a חטאת, because its blood goes above. Can you say it about an אשם?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר's comparison. He points to a way the חטאת is stricter than the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the source has no special strictness of its own. The חטאת's blood goes above the red line, but the אשם's goes below. So the strict rule of שלא לשמה might come from that special feature, and it would not carry over to the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say this about... (you can't compare)
Since, because it has
Its blood is put above the red line on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No;
if you say so regarding a sin offering,
that is because its blood is placed above!
phrases.notes: He means above the red line around the מזבח. The אשם's blood goes below it, so the two are not alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's comparison of אשם to חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חטאת has a stricter feature (blood above) that אשם lacks, so the rule cannot be carried over.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: פסח proves the point
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers with פסח. Its blood goes below, yet it is still invalid שלא לשמו, so blood going above is not the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: Let the פסח prove it. Its blood goes below, and if one slaughtered it שלא לשמו, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his view by bringing a second example, the פסח. It shows that blood going above is not needed for the strict rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said the strict rule might depend on blood going above. But פסח's blood goes below, and it is still invalid שלא לשמו. So the rule does not depend on that feature, and the אשם, whose blood also goes below, can share it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Pesach offering
Will prove it, serves as proof
Below the red line on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
Let the Paschal offering prove it,
for its blood is placed below,
and if one slaughtered it not for its sake, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: פֶּסַח יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example showing that the challenged feature is not what causes the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict rule of שלא לשמה might depend on blood going above, as with חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח, whose blood goes below, is also invalid, so blood going above is not the reason.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: פסח has a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the proof from פסח. פסח has its own stricter feature, a fixed time, which the אשם does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: What about פסח? It has a fixed time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back again. He shows that the פסח also has a special strict feature, so it cannot serve as a source for the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח can only be brought at one set time each year, and an אשם has no fixed time. So פסח's strict rule might come from that feature instead. Now each example has its own strictness, and neither one alone proves anything about the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (pointing to a special feature that blocks the comparison)
Its time is fixed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר tried to learn אשם from חטאת and then from פסח. רבי יהושע blocked each one by finding a stricter feature: חטאת's blood goes above, and פסח has a fixed time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
What about the Paschal offering?
It is special, since its time is fixed!
phrases.notes: An אשם can be brought any time, so it does not share this stricter feature.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מָה לְפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from פסח given in step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פסח has its own strict feature, a fixed time, that the אשם lacks, so it cannot be the source.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר Points Back to the Sin Offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers the rejection of פסח by pointing to חטאת. It has no fixed time, yet it is still invalid שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: The חטאת proves the point.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his position. He says the חטאת shows that a fixed time is not what makes an offering invalid שלא לשמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had said פסח is different because it has a fixed time. רבי אליעזר answers that a חטאת has no fixed time, yet it is still invalid שלא לשמו. So the fixed time cannot be the reason, and the אשם should share the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove; this case shows the point
A fixed time, the special feature of פסח
Offered with the wrong purpose in mind, not for its own sake

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר is going back to his first argument. Earlier, רבי יהושע rejected חטאת because its blood goes on the upper part of the מזבח. Here חטאת answers a different objection, the fixed time of פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
A sin offering can prove it.
phrases.notes: He means the חטאת has no fixed time, yet it is still invalid שלא לשמו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: חַטָּאת תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה of step 22, which said פסח is stricter because it has a fixed time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example: a case without the stricter feature still has the same rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fixed time of פסח might be the reason it is invalid שלא לשמו, so the אשם, which has no fixed time, would not learn from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חטאת has no fixed time and is still invalid שלא לשמו, so a fixed time is not the deciding reason.

steps.title: רבי יהושע Begins His Reply
steps.stepSummary: The text opens רבי יהושע's response to רבי אליעזר's new argument. His actual words come on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. It tells us רבי יהושע is about to answer, but his words come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, each side has rejected the other's proof by pointing out something special about it. This line signals that רבי יהושע will now respond to the חטאת argument. We have to wait for the next lines to hear what he says.
